figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The x-axis label says 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)', but the subtitle and caption say '140 GB tensor' without repeating 'per rank'. A reader can misread 140 GB as the total tensor size rather than the per-rank input size, which changes the arithmetic by a factor of N.
evidence: Figure subtitle: '140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75×)'. Caption: 'At 140 GB the ideal times are about 0.54 s, 6.1 s and 98 s.' The x-axis is 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)'. The 1.75× factor is 2(N−1)/N for N=8, so 140 GB must be per rank for 245 GB sent per rank to be correct.
acceptance_test: Change the subtitle and caption to say '140 GB per rank' or '140 GB logical tensor per rank' everywhere the 140 GB operating point is named; verify no remaining sentence can be read as 140 GB total.

issue: The annotation text '3 neighbor rounds' and '6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' is visibly smaller than the rank labels and array values and appears to fall below the 8 pt print floor at final trim size.
evidence: In the rendered 150 dpi page, the annotation text is approximately 70% the height of the main figure labels. At 150 dpi, 8 pt is about 16.7 px; these annotations appear closer to 14 px. The figure is otherwise legible, but the smallest annotations are the ones carrying the byte-count reasoning.
acceptance_test: Measure the PDF font size of the two annotation strings. If any is below 8 pt, raise it to at least 8 pt and re-render; confirm no overlap with the vertical arrows or phase labels.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The text inside the layer boxes is too small for comfortable print reading. The figure packs four layers, two implementation columns, and multiple lines per box into a single page-width diagram; several box lines appear below the 8 pt floor.
evidence: At 150 dpi, the box text 'CUDA device execution', 'GPU P2P / shared memory', 'SYCL / Level Zero path', and 'Actual path depends on build' is visibly smaller than the surrounding body text and smaller than the figure's layer labels. The diagram is dense enough that the reader must work to decode the layout before understanding the payload-versus-setup distinction.
acceptance_test: Measure every text span inside the numbered layer boxes. Raise all to at least 8 pt, or split the figure into two panels (NVIDIA path and oneCCL path) with a shared setup legend. Re-render and confirm no box text is clipped or crowded.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The layer labels '1 Framework backend', '2 Collective library and algorithm', '3 Device runtime plus transport', and '4 Physical resources and topology' are left-aligned above the NVIDIA column only. They visually appear to label the left stack, not both columns, even though the right column is at the same layer.
evidence: The labels sit above the left-hand boxes and do not span or center over the two-column layout. The right-hand boxes are vertically aligned with the left-hand boxes, but the labels do not visually bind them to the same layer.
acceptance_test: Center each layer label across both columns, or add a left-margin bracket that clearly spans both columns at each numbered layer. Confirm a reader can see at a glance that ProcessGroupNCCL and ProcessGroupXCCL are both layer 1, NCCL and oneCCL are both layer 2, and so on.

issue: The dashed red control/setup arrows are thin and low-contrast against the light red fill of the top box. In grayscale they may read as faint gray dashes, weakening the visual separation between setup and payload.
evidence: The legend distinguishes solid black payload arrows from dashed red setup arrows. The dashed arrows from the top 'Launcher, rank/device mapping, rendezvous' box to the ProcessGroup boxes are the only red elements in the diagram and are visually lighter than the solid black payload arrows.
acceptance_test: Check the figure in grayscale at print size. If the dashed setup arrows are not immediately distinguishable from the solid payload arrows, increase their stroke weight or use a darker dash pattern while preserving the legend distinction.
